concept: Cloud exit-credit programs and EU Data Act in-parallel egress
summary: Source-anchored research for Cloud exit-credit programs and EU Data Act in-parallel egress. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: AWS exit credits apply only to qualifying internet data transfer out, excluding standard service charges and specialized transfer services such as Direct Connect, CloudFront, Snow Family and Global Accelerator. AWS may reclaim credits when the traffic did not support the qualifying departure. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-26)

A June 2026 Toulouse School of Economics working-paper abstract reports that egress-fee regulation improves user surplus in its two-period duopoly model, while an outright ban can reduce total welfare when transfer or operational switching costs are high. This is a model result, not an empirical estimate of migration savings. (low confidence)

Google's exit process requires an Exit Notice before migration, an initial 14-day period, initiation within the next 30 days, and a subsequent migration period of at least 30 days with extension provisions. Credits appear on final invoices after the data recovery period; transfers during that recovery period are not eligible migration transfers. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-09-11)

Google's final-invoice credit and Azure's post-completion credit (applied only after the data transfer is complete and all Azure subscriptions are canceled) show that an egress concession can arrive after usage is billed. Treat the credit's cash-flow timing separately from the eventual net transfer cost when planning a cutover. Sources: https://cloud.google.com/exit-cloud ; https://mc.merill.net/message/AZ-now-available-free-data-transfer-out-to-internet-when-leaving-azure ; https://www.itpro.com/cloud/cloud-computing/microsoft-scraps-egress-fees-for-azure-was-its-hand-forced-by-google-and-aws

Article 29 phases out switching charges, including switching-related data egress, from 12 January 2027. Before that deadline, permissible reduced switching charges cannot exceed directly related switching costs. This is a switching rule, not a universal abolition of network charges. (high confidence) Sources: https://externer-datenschutzbeauftragter-dresden.de/gesetze/en/data-act/p-29 ; https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/factpages/data-act-explained ; https://externer-datenschutzbeauftragter-dresden.de/gesetze/en/data-act/p-34

Article 34(2) permits egress charges for in-parallel use only to pass through incurred egress costs, without a premium. Unlike the Article 29 switching-charge prohibition, this parallel-use cost cap does not expire in January 2027. (high confidence) Sources: https://externer-datenschutzbeauftragter-dresden.de/gesetze/en/data-act/p-34 ; https://externer-datenschutzbeauftragter-dresden.de/gesetze/en/data-act/p-29 ; https://bundesnetzagentur.de/EN/Areas/Digitalisation/DataAct/background/3-provider/start.html

Azure's parallel-use offering is at cost rather than necessarily free. Its documentation limits eligibility to organizations billed in the EEA, EFTA or UK with qualifying regional data storage; customers supply destination ASNs and traffic percentages through support, and validated refunds continue in future billing cycles. Routing qualifications apply, with a separate UK allowance for Microsoft's global network. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-05-05)

AWS’s currently served exit programme requires a support request at least two months before the planned start and approval before transfer. It supports either a complete exit or moving all data from a particular AWS service across eligible accounts; it requires deletion from the departed services by completion. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-26)

Google’s exit page, last updated 11 September 2025, describes an Exit Notice, initiation and migration periods, a Completion Notice, and termination of the relevant service agreement. Other services may continue. The qualifying transfer credit appears on final invoices after the Data Recovery Period; production data moved during that recovery period is excluded. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-09-11)

Google explicitly separates exit credits from continued service use and points European customers to Data Transfer Essentials for parallel use. Its current overview initially offers qualifying traffic at no charge, requires configuration of supported services and destination IPs/ASNs, and excludes traffic serving external customers. Invalid destinations can revert to ordinary internet billing. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-26) Sources: https://cloud.google.com/exit-cloud ; https://docs.cloud.google.com/data-transfer-essentials/docs/overview

Azure’s 5 May 2026 guidance offers at-cost parallel-use transfers for qualifying EEA/EFTA/UK organizations, with regional and network-route restrictions. The customer supplies subscription ID, destination ASN and estimated traffic percentage in a support request; Azure validates it and applies refunds to the next bill and future cycles. Endpoints must belong to the same organization. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-05-05)

An Azure user thread reports difficulty obtaining a usable advance at-cost unit price after contacting support. This is a firsthand report of quotation friction, not evidence of a universal Azure rate or proof that every customer receives the same response. (low confidence)

For migration budgeting, record the gross transfer charge, expected qualifying credit and credit timing separately. AWS describes temporary transfer credits, while Google applies the qualifying credit on final invoices after its recovery period; a waived net egress cost need not imply the same billing timeline. (medium confidence) Sources: https://aws.amazon.com/ec2/faqs/ ; https://cloud.google.com/exit-cloud

Cost estimates should retain ordinary service charges during overlap and test ongoing cross-cloud replication separately from one-time exit traffic. This budgeting recommendation follows from AWS’s service-charge exclusion and Google’s explicit separation of exit credits from ongoing parallel use. (medium confidence) Sources: https://aws.amazon.com/ec2/faqs/ ; https://cloud.google.com/exit-cloud

The German regulator describes a normal switching transition of at most 30 calendar days after a notice period of at most two months, with permitted extensions and at least 30 days of post-switch retrieval. The regulator permits extensions to the normal switching transition under specified conditions. (low confidence)

AWS's exit program covers moving all data off AWS across eligible accounts or all data off a particular AWS service across eligible accounts; Google likewise requires ending all use of the relevant service. Neither program should be budgeted as an unconditional waiver for a partial service exit or indefinite parallel operation. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) Sources: https://aws.amazon.com/ec2/faqs/ ; https://cloud.google.com/exit-cloud

AWS's FAQ requires contacting support at least two months before the planned switch initiation and obtaining credit approval before starting. The temporary credit applies only to eligible data transfer out, excludes ordinary service consumption and specialized transfer services such as Direct Connect, and may be reversed if the transfer was not for the qualifying exit. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-26)

AWS's 8 October 2026 update gives eligible customers outside the EU 180 days to complete their exit and directs EU customers exercising Data Act rights to the EU Data Act Addendum. Older accounts of a universal 60-day completion window should not be used as current program guidance. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-08) Sources: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/free-data-transfer-out-to-internet-when-moving-out-of-aws/ ; https://datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/aws-removes-some-data-transfer-fees-for-customers-exiting-its-cloud

Google treats ongoing parallel use separately from its exit-credit program. Data Transfer Essentials configures eligible cross-cloud traffic for services belonging to the same organization; its overview says the offering is initially free, may become billed with advance notice, and has no SLA. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-26) Sources: https://cloud.google.com/exit-cloud ; https://docs.cloud.google.com/data-transfer-essentials/docs/overview

Both Google's Data Transfer Essentials and Azure's parallel-use offering distinguish traffic within the same organization from delivery to third-party customers. Do not assume that application delivery to end users or CDN traffic qualifies for the parallel-use concession. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-26) Sources: https://docs.cloud.google.com/data-transfer-essentials/docs/overview ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cost-management-billing/manage/data-transfer-fees ; https://docs.cloud.google.com/data-transfer-essentials/docs/faq

A migration cost model should keep ordinary service fees and contractual early-termination liabilities separate from eligible switching egress. The Data Act does not make normal service consumption free, and AWS's exit credit expressly excludes standard service charges. (medium confidence) Sources: https://prighter.com/resources/laws/data-act/articles/article-2 ; https://prighter.com/resources/laws/data-act/articles/article-29 ; https://aws.amazon.com/ec2/faqs/
